title: Compact support and coefficient extension retain the finite-Tor domain
statement: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $h:U\to V$ be a separated finite-type map of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with compactification $U\xrightarrow jW\xrightarrow rV$ in the same class [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $N_T=\nu_T^*$ for site pullback [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $E_B=E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ for coefficient extension on either site [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Let $L\in D^b(U_{\rm et},A)$ have constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning a uniform finite cohomology interval for its tensor with each degree-zero module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Put $F_R^{\rm et}=Rr_{*,R}^{\rm et}j_{!,R}^{\rm et}$ and $F_R^{\rm pro}=Rr_{*,R}^{\rm pro}j_{!,R}^{\rm pro}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Then $F_A^{\rm et}L$ and $F_B^{\rm et}(L_B)$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, and so are their site pullbacks, with intrinsically constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude on the pro-etale site [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. The complexes $(F_A^{\rm et}L)_B$ and $L_B$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude as well. The specified map $N_VF_R^{\rm et}E\to F_R^{\rm pro}N_UE$ obtained by the proper counit mate and the open comparison is an isomorphism for every bounded-below etale input $E$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Consequently all these inputs and actual scalar extensions lie in $D^+$; no finite projective dimension of $B/A$ is assumed. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), finite-Tor domains for coefficient and composite inputs. Agent reflection argument from the named comparison theorems.
